definition: His share of the air yards his team's passes travelled toward targets, in the games he played (the usage layer's definition). Pooled over the games he played: his total divided by his team's total in those games, keyed by the club he played for that week.
Official receptions. Official nflverse box-score total.
His share of his team's offensive snaps in the games he played, pooled over snaps. Team snaps are taken from the player on the field for the most snaps.

His share of his team's targets in the games he played (the usage layer's definition). Pooled over the games he played: his total divided by his team's total in those games, keyed by the club he played for that week.
Official targets: passes thrown to him. Official nflverse box-score total.
Receptions per target — not his share of the team's catches. Uncatchable throws count as targets.
Yards gained after the catch, per reception (nflverse's unofficial YAC).
Yards after the catch beyond what Next Gen Stats' tracking model expected from where defenders were at the catch, per reception.
Official receiving touchdowns. Official nflverse box-score total.
Official receiving yards. Official nflverse box-score total.
Expected points added per target: catches, first downs, touchdowns, drops and interceptions on throws to him all count.
His share of his team's targets inside the 20 in the games he played.
Targets on plays snapped inside the opponent's 20-yard line.
Targets thrown far enough to reach the goal line (air yards at least the distance to the end zone). Derived; nflverse has no end-zone flag.
How far past the line of scrimmage passes to him travel on average, caught or not (official receiving air yards per target).
Average distance to the nearest defender at the moment of the catch or the incompletion, on his targets only.
His 40-yard dash time at the NFL Scouting Combine, in the year he tested, ranked among every tester at the same combine position since 2000 with a recorded time (faster ranks first).
A game played is a regular-season week with a weekly stats row or at least one offensive snap (the usage layer's and season actuals' definition).
interpretation: How much of the downfield passing game runs through him.
How much of the game he is on the field for.
How much of the passing game is aimed at him when he plays.
How often a throw to him became a catch.
Yardage produced per throw his way.
What he adds once the ball is in his hands.
What he gains after the catch that the situation did not give him.
How much each throw to him moved his team's expected score.
How much of the red-zone passing game is aimed at him.
His receiving role where touchdowns are scored.
A role reading: deep threat or underneath target. Neither is better.
Context, not a skill score: deep and contested targets carry less separation by design, and it says nothing about routes that were not thrown to.
Historical athletic context from before his NFL career. It is not a measurement of his current on-field speed.
Every other number in the tree is counted over these games only.
limitations: Negative air yards (behind the line) reduce both sides.
Regular season through the board's cutoff week, summed over the games he played.
Snaps are not routes or touches. A game the snap file has no row for him in is left out of both sides. Differs from the usage rails' per-game average.
Counts targets, not routes; a decoy on the field is not in it.
Regular season through the board's cutoff week, summed over the games he played.

Only for receivers Next Gen Stats qualifies (wide receivers and tight ends) and only when its season summary matches his official targets through the cutoff.
Touchdowns are rare events; small differences are noise.
Regular season through the board's cutoff week, summed over the games he played.

Shared with the quarterback and the play call. Efficiency rates are noisy early in a season: in 2023-2025 the weeks 1-5 rate of this kind related only weakly to the rest of the same season (EDA 2026-10-14). It describes his games so far, not what comes next.
Small denominators early in the season.
A count; it depends on how often his team reaches the red zone.
Air yards are measured to where the ball was caught or targeted.
Targets only, not every route; not proof of isolated receiver skill. Only for receivers Next Gen Stats qualifies.
Linked only through nflverse's PFR-to-GSIS identity bridge; players who did not run at the combine, or whose combine row cannot be linked unambiguously, have no time. Pro-day times are not included.
Byes and missed weeks are not games; a game is counted however few snaps.
